problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $f(x),$ defined below?

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2},\, & x\le 1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x),\, & x>1\end{aligned}
$$

- $f(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=1$
- $f(x)$ is right-continuous at $x=1$
- $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $h(x),$ defined below?

$$
h(x)={\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-27,\, & x<3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2),\, & x\ge 3\end{aligned}
$$

- $h(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=3$
- $h(x)$ is right-continuous at $x=3$
- $h(x)$ is continuous at $x=3$
feedback.worked_solution:
We're required to determine the left and right continuity properties of $h(x)$ at $x=3.$

Let's start by computing $h(3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}h(3) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-2) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is true. The function is left-continuous at $x=3$ since the left-sided limit is equal to the function value:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}h(x) & ={3}^{3}-27 \\  & =27-27 \\  & =0 \\  & =h(3)\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is true. The function is right-continuous at $x=3$ since the right-sided limit is equal to the function value:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {3}^{+}}h(x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-2) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\  & =0 \\  & =h(3)\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is true. The function is both left and right-continuous at $x=3,$ which implies that the function is continuous at $x=3.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."
